evidenceRecords.statement: The catchment NDVI area median was 0.1439 in April 2022.

limitations: Written from a synthetic replay, not a model output or a live model call.
Reduced QA (scene classification only): snow, snow edges and terrain shadow can survive the mask.
In winter months the accepted pixels favour the valley floor and south-facing slopes, because snow and shade remove the others; the area value then describes those pixels, not the whole catchment.
The spatial IQR is variability across pixels, not a confidence interval.
No cropland or irrigation mask is applied in this version: valley-floor fields and orchards are inside the summary.
Processing baselines differ across the record (mostly 05.00 for 2019 to 2021, 04.00 for 2022, 05.09 to 05.11 later); same-acquisition comparisons differ by about 0.002 to 0.003 reflectance.
Seven years is a short record; nothing here is a trend or a degradation finding.
Cloud and snow shares are counted per tile observation; the 29SQR and 29RQQ overlap counts twice.

Revision 13 (2026-10-27). Among duplicates of a tile and date, an item with no clear pixels over the catchment is now skipped when a twin has some. That clause was added to the duplicate rule after data was first read; the rule fixed before any data was read kept the newest processing baseline only. Revision 12, the first committed, has no version field; it documented the clause but kept the newest item, so it kept an item with 0 clear pixels over the catchment on seven tile-dates: 29RQQ 2019-04-17 (twin had 285 clear pixels), 2019-06-21 (702,669), 2020-11-12 (84), 2021-06-07 (8), 2021-11-19 (8), 2021-12-22 (8), and 29SQR 2020-10-23 (16). In five cases the twin is an older baseline (02.14, 03.00, 03.01), so its clear pixels come from an older scene classification. This revision recomputes 2019-04, 2019-06, 2020-10, 2020-11, 2021-06, 2021-11 and 2021-12 and everything derived from them; no NDVI or departure area median moved at four decimals.

evidenceRecords.uncertainty: Spatial IQR across pixels is shown with each value; it is variability, not a confidence interval.
